### Observed differences

- In the earlier window A01 occurred in every trace (200 of 200) and almost always as the first event (median position 0, mean about 0.1); in the later window A01 does not appear in a single trace, and none of its outgoing transitions — about 46 in 100 went to A03, 34 to A04, 16 to A02, with small shares to A05 and A06 — are observed. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001]
- A04 was present in about 51 in 100 earlier traces, around the middle of the trace (mean position about 0.41), followed mostly by A02 (about 70 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) and A06 (about 19 in 100); in the later window A04 is not observed at all and has no observed outgoing transitions. [OCC002, POS004, DIR003]
- Earlier, A03 and A04 were strict alternatives (about 49 vs 51 in 100 traces, never together); in the later window A03 still occurs, in about 53 in 100 traces, while A04 is gone and about 47 in 100 traces contain neither. [REL005, POS003]
- The surviving branch activities moved to the front: A03 now occurs only as the first event (mean position 0, previously about 0.44) and A02 likewise (mean position 0, previously about 0.53), while their trace shares stayed roughly stable (A03 about 49% to 53%, A02 about 51% to 47%); together they account for essentially every later trace. [POS003, POS002]
- A02's routing narrowed: earlier, about 79 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions went to A06 (the rest to A04, about 14, and A01, about 7); in the later window every observed outgoing transition of A02 goes to A06. [DIR002]
- A06 lost its loop-back edges: earlier, in the 14 traces where A06 was followed by another activity, it led back to A04 (about 71 in 100) or A01 (about 29 in 100); in the later window A06 is never observed with a successor, although A02 → A06 still occurs, so A06 now appears only at the end of traces. [DIR004, DIR002]
- All relations involving A01 collapsed: co-occurrence with A02 fell from 51% to 0, with A03 from 49% to 0 and with A04 from 51% to 0, and A02 and A03 now occur only without A01. [REL001, REL002, REL003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that in the later window the process no longer executes its opening activity A01 nor the A04 step: A01, which appeared in every earlier trace (200 of 200), and A04, present in about 51 in 100 earlier traces, are unobserved in all 200 later traces. Traces now begin directly with A02 (about 47 in 100) or A03 (about 53 in 100) — the same branch activities that previously followed A01 — and A02 leads only to A06, which now ends the trace instead of occasionally returning control to A04 or A01. Because A01 and A04 are absent from the later window, this is a structural difference (an opening activity and a branch no longer executed), not a re-weighting of paths that all remain observed. [OCC001, OCC002, POS002, POS003, DIR002, DIR004, REL005]

The screening context makes chance an unlikely explanation: 15 control-flow items qualified where roughly 0.1 would be expected without a change, and the occurrence, position, direction and relation indicators all describe the same difference (A01 participation 100% to 0%, A04 51% to 0%, A02 and A03 moving to first position, A02→A06 from 79% to 100%, all A01 relations falling from 49–51% to 0%). [OCC001, OCC002, POS002, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, REL001, REL002, REL003]

Limitations: zero participation establishes only that A01 and A04 were not observed, not that they were removed from the underlying process — they may still exist but be skipped in every later case. The evidence also does not describe what follows A03 in the later window (the qualified directional items cover only A01, A02, A04 and A06), and the rare edge from A01 to A05 (about 3 in 100 of A01's outgoing transitions earlier) is uncharacterised for the later window. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
